Message:
manager: land 21 checklist items the operator's page never saw, and the dirty-PR recurrence that hid them (#12476)

* manager: land 21 checklist items, MI-318 dispatch, and the dirty-PR recurrence

The manager branch had accumulated 36 commits behind a SILENT blocker: PR
#12476 read `mergeable_state: dirty` for 14.5h, and a dirty PR builds no merge
ref, so it ran ZERO check runs -- which renders identically to "CI has not
started" and to "all green". Nothing went red, so nothing paged.

The operator-facing cost is the part that matters: MI-298..MI-318 (21 items)
existed only on this branch, and GET /api/bot/work/checklist reads the VM's
working tree, which tracks main. So the live Workflow page -- the artifact the
operator asked for on 2026-09-10 precisely so they could track lanes without
pulling detail into chat -- had never seen any of them. The rule is "push, then
answer"; the push happened, to a branch the page does not read.

Filed as a RECURRENCE (commit 129c632a9, two days earlier, is titled "the lease
lapsed because my heartbeats landed on a branch whose PR had already merged"),
because the fix that did not hold was "the manager remembers to land its
branch" -- a habit, not a mechanism.

CONFLICT RESOLUTION, by hand, because merge_json_register correctly REFUSED to
guess on MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json:
  * items: strict three-way per id. Verified first that NO item was changed on
    both sides -- 53 changed only on main (MI-237's `state` backfill, #12525),
    3 only here, 21 new here -- so the merge is unambiguous rather than a
    judgement call.
  * `_lane_queues`: this branch rewrote the block wholesale while main ADDED
    `ops.pr_queue_noise_measurement_2026_09_18T0715Z`. A wholesale rewrite
    silently deletes a sibling's addition, which is why the refusal was right.
    Carried main's measurement forward, and restored `lane_assignment_provenance`
    from base -- three recorded operator lane decisions this branch had dropped.
  * AND THAT MEASUREMENT ANSWERS A QUESTION THIS BRANCH STILL LISTED AS OPEN:
    the ops queue's next item read "clause (1) ... Unestablished", but MI-315
    established it on main at 07:15Z -- stale-automation-sweep.yml is FIRED AND
    SUCCEEDING ON SCHEDULE. Without the conflict forcing a comparison, a lane
    would have been dispatched to re-derive it.
  * WO-20260918-PER-LEG-TARGET-GEOMETRY-PROPOSAL-AT-STATED-N: add/add. Took
    main's -- the research lane actually did the work and closed it `done`;
    this branch held a dispatch stub marked `in_flight`.

⚠️ R6 FIRED ON A REAL VIOLATION OF MINE AND IS NOT BEING ROUTED AROUND.
check_manager_scope R6 failed commit b59681df: it advanced the lease heartbeat
while SESSIONS.json was 95 minutes stale against a 90-minute TTL -- a manager
holding a lease longer than its own supervision record. That is not a false
positive; it is the same failure the operator caught independently the same
morning ("why are lanes idle?"), and the guard saw it first. The
manager-scope-exception file is PATH-scoped and would have been the wrong tool
-- using it here would be lying to a guard, which this repo names as worse than
no guard. So the branch is squashed instead (every commit on it is mine, no
other session's work is at risk) and the violation is recorded HERE, in prose,
rather than being erased along with the commit that carried it.

Also in this change:
  * MI-318 dispatched: decision pop-ups never arrive because every prompt over
    Telegram's 4096-char cap 400s, forever, on a 5-minute retry. Measured with
    a positive control (4738/4569/5463 chars failing; a 3815-char request
    delivered). Lane spawned on claude-sonnet-5, chosen and recorded with its
    reason rather than inherited.
  * MI-312's object closed: the lane REFUTED the dispatch premise, and that
    refutation is the finding.
  * Lease re-claimed by the same holder, with the unrefreshable case stated.

* manager: make the three blocked decision prompts fit the Telegram cap

The operator asked for the decisions as pop-ups twice. They cannot be sent:
every prompt renders over Telegram's 4096-char sendMessage cap and 400s,
forever, on a 5-minute retry.

MEASURED per component, which is what makes this fixable without touching code:
the QUESTION is 370-441 chars and the CONTEXT is 2181 / 2557 / 3554. The context
is what blows the cap, and the context is DATA in this work object, not the
renderer.

So each request's long context is preserved VERBATIM under a new `context_full`
key and `context` is replaced with a compact version carrying the decisive
facts, the traps, and a pointer to the full text. The renderer inlines `context`
only, so the prompt now fits:

  DEC-20260913-FOUR-LEG-DISPOSITION                4738 -> 4002  (headroom  94)
  DEC-20260917-SCALP-MARGIN-BOUND-SIZING           5463 -> 3711  (headroom 385)
  DEC-20260917-NETTING-ATTRIBUTION-...-DROPPABLE   4569 -> 3633  (headroom 463)

All three keep their full option set and tappable keyboard, and `callback_data`
is untouched at 26 bytes -- the key-digest guarantee that stops a reordered
option recording the wrong answer is not weakened.

VERIFIED, not assumed: every other field (question, options, notes, asked_by,
urgency, blocking) is byte-identical after parse; the original context is
verbatim as `context_full`; the only added key is `context_full`; and the diff
is 60 insertions / 0 deletions, so nothing was removed from the file. The first
splice attempt reformatted all 1744 lines and was reverted rather than shipped.

⚠️ THIS IS NOT THE FIX AND MUST NOT BE READ AS ONE. MI-318 owns the renderer's
missing compaction ladder, and that lane is running. This unblocks the four
questions in flight; the next over-cap prompt written by anyone else fails
exactly as these did until MI-318 lands.

⚠️ AND IT DOES NOT SHORTEN A QUESTION. MI-318's must_not forbids that, correctly
-- editing a decision's wording to make a transport bug go away would corrupt the
record of what was asked. Only CONTEXT moved, which that object's own
done_condition names as the compactable part.

* manager: MI-318 closed as a duplicate of MI-303 — my dispatch error

The lane returned COMPLETED having closed its own PR as a duplicate of #12490,
and I verified that rather than taking the summary. #12490 (MI-303) was opened
2026-09-17T23:36Z, is Tier-2 `landing: hold`, and diagnoses the identical defect
with BETTER evidence than my dispatch produced -- a partition over the complete
population of 33 decision requests against the live marker file, two positive

both times was "the fix is written and waiting on your merge click plus a bot
restart", not a new lane. Cost: ~$23.76 to re-derive a held PR.

⚠️ THE DEFECT IS STILL LIVE ON MAIN -- `grep -c 4096` on origin/main's renderer
reads 0, measured after the lane closed. A closed duplicate fixes nothing.

registers as #11860. Serially they produce three conflicts and three

based on #11860's tip and carries both payloads, so the two are redundant
and are closed rather than resolved.

    operator_decisions_0540Z, lane_roster_0548Z). Asserted disjoint from
    the keys already present; no existing key altered.
  - SESSIONS.json: 229 + 228 -> 231 by id-union. Asserted every shared row
    byte-identical, so the two new rows (MI-281, MI-282) are the whole delta.
  - the two lane-4/5 work objects.

And one correction that is not a fold:

THE WORK STORE SAID 2 IN FLIGHT WHILE SIX LANES WERE RUNNING. All five
objects dispatched today sat `lifecycle: dormant` with `owner: null` and
`blocked_on_basis: NOT_ASSESSED` — the capture-time default — because
capture_idea.py parks an idea and nothing moves it when a session is
actually given it. So the constraint computation, whose whole input is
lifecycle plus typed edges, was reading a store that understated the live
WIP by a factor of three.

Each of the five now carries `in_flight`, the real session id as `owner`,
and an ASSESSED basis. The basis is a POSITIVE finding, not a bulk
NOT_ASSESSED sweep: for each row the claim is that nothing blocks it TODAY
because a named session is running it, read off list_sessions rather than
inferred from the registry. No blocked_on edge is invented. Where a Tier-2
or Tier-3 gate is expected later in a lane's queue it is deliberately NOT
written now — an anticipated blocker is a false blocker until the work
reaches it, and a false blocker is worse than a missing one.

content, so the manager opens a follow-up -- and branching from the armed

commit's two parents -- here there is no merge commit at all.

roster read with a fresher date. No lease heartbeat here either: 08:18:18Z is
already stamped in #11773, which is in flight, and a second write would put two
lease claims in two open PRs.

What did change is that I dispatched the thing I named last report as owed.

SPAWNED THE OPS LANE (session_01NFnmLiu9zNDppY3qFXcJJA) to disposition the 17
unsupported in_flight rows. The WIP ceiling of 8 is FULL and four of its eight
object slots are unsupported, held by owners dormant 34.8-37.9h — so the ceiling
is no longer a guideline, it is the binding constraint on ALL further work,
trading work included. Nothing new can start until it clears, and three lanes
were sitting idle against it.

The ops role covers this by the operator's own wording: "unsticking what is
stuck" is placed above the ops backlog, so this competes with nothing.

WHAT THE LANE ADDS OVER MI-236, and the distinction is the whole point: MI-236's
lane graded OWNERS and refused to recommend a landing state, because that needs
each row read against its own done_condition. This is that reading — per ROW.
The refusal is inherited rather than overridden; what changes is that someone
does the reading that makes a landing state establishable.

Its prompt carries the harm explicitly: a lower unsupported count is trivially
achievable by marking rows done, `done` means MERGED AND OBSERVED, and a
terminal owner says the work will not resume rather than that it finished. It
is also told to disposition ROWS and not to start the work they describe —
several are substantial, and taking one would be the drop pattern one level up —
and not to file a wip-ceiling-exception, since clearing the ceiling honestly is
the job.

spurious decay marks live work abandoned, a spurious wake only costs a turn —
and NOT to auto-close a decayed row, because that is a claim about an OWNER and
not about the WORK, and guessing the landing state destroys the "where do we
pick this up" record.

changes_landing_machinery, and the distinction from #11752 is the point: that
one was held because the guard could not certify its TIER by path, a question I
could and did answer off the diff. This one is held because the CATEGORY is the
landing machinery itself, which is the last thing an automated actor should wave
through. No approval is outstanding; it needs a human read.

Two things I got wrong in this tick, both caught before they landed: a backtick
in a --why argument was substituted by the shell and silently dropped the
registration, and I wrote the work object's id into the exception file with a
suffix capture_idea.py had not used. The register call reported nothing amiss —
I found both by checking that the row I expected actually existed.

Supervision is a REAL live read this time, which the previous commit said was
owed after carrying an inferred count.

MULTI_STRATEGY_INTENT_LAYER=false routes to a SECOND builder registry holding 16

(pending-20260909T230624Z) and confirmed after, which is the order MI-15 exists
to enforce.

The prompt carries the operator's answer verbatim: DELETING the second registry
is the point, and a parity test alone is explicitly not it — that option was
offered and the operator chose the collapse over it. It also scopes the lane OFF
src/units/accounts/execute.py and scripts/ops/system_invariants.py, and forbids
flipping MULTI_STRATEGY_INTENT_LAYER on the live VM: the fix is the code path,

Message:
I spawned MI-205 into the wrong repository; interrupt, re-dispatch, route the prevention

MI-205 was seeded with source_url omitted and attached
the-lizardking/ict-trading-bot -- a different OWNER, outside this session's
allowed scope. It reached RUNNING, cloned that repo, read its docs and
pushed a board START there before I interrupted it at 22:17Z. Re-dispatched
as MI-205b (session_01ML8uLRrKLMmzR9fFywTWv5) with the source pinned to
benbaichmankass/metis-insights. Nothing was lost from this repo and nothing
MI-205 produced is recoverable.

I caught it only because I went looking for whether the child had actually
STARTED rather than assuming it had. get_session returns
session_context.sources in one call.

The trap is in the tool's own wording: create_session says it inherits the
calling session's ENVIRONMENT when environment_id is omitted, and an
environment is not a set of SOURCES. Verified both directions -- my own
session carries the three benbaichmankass/* repos, while MI-205, spawned
from it in the same environment, carried the-lizardking one.

NO BACKLOG ROW WAS FILED, DELIBERATELY. The class is already filed three
times and the third row's resolution_criteria says in terms: "NOT
SUFFICIENT: another backlog row, another line in a spawn template." It
measures 15 instances across 5 days and records that filing taught nothing.
Mine is the 16th. A fourth row would be the accumulation the repo complains
about.

What IS new is that I spawned THROUGH session_registry.py and register and
confirm BOTH SUCCEEDED -- the registry records that a spawn happened and
cannot see which repo the child was handed, so a registered spawn is not a
correctly-targeted one. The registry is also the one thing in this class the
repo actually owns, since nothing here sits on create_session's call path.
Routed as MI-207: refuse to register without an explicit --source-url, and
print it into the spawn prompt the registry already emits. It is a scripts/
change, so it goes to a session, not to me.

MI-205 was seeded with source_url omitted and attached
the-lizardking/ict-trading-bot -- a different OWNER, outside this session's
allowed scope. It reached RUNNING, cloned that repo, read its docs and
pushed a board START there before I interrupted it at 22:17Z. Re-dispatched
as MI-205b (session_01ML8uLRrKLMmzR9fFywTWv5) with the source pinned to
benbaichmankass/metis-insights. Nothing was lost from this repo and nothing
MI-205 produced is recoverable.

I caught it only because I went looking for whether the child had actually
STARTED rather than assuming it had. get_session returns
session_context.sources in one call.

The trap is in the tool's own wording: create_session says it inherits the
calling session's ENVIRONMENT when environment_id is omitted, and an
environment is not a set of SOURCES. Verified both directions -- my own
session carries the three benbaichmankass/* repos, while MI-205, spawned
from it in the same environment, carried the-lizardking one.

NO BACKLOG ROW WAS FILED, DELIBERATELY. The class is already filed three
times and the third row's resolution_criteria says in terms: "NOT
SUFFICIENT: another backlog row, another line in a spawn template." It
measures 15 instances across 5 days and records that filing taught nothing.
Mine is the 16th. A fourth row would be the accumulation the repo complains
about.

What IS new is that I spawned THROUGH session_registry.py and register and
confirm BOTH SUCCEEDED -- the registry records that a spawn happened and
cannot see which repo the child was handed, so a registered spawn is not a
correctly-targeted one. The registry is also the one thing in this class the
repo actually owns, since nothing here sits on create_session's call path.
Routed as MI-207: refuse to register without an explicit --source-url, and
print it into the spawn prompt the registry already emits. It is a scripts/
change, so it goes to a session, not to me.

MI-173 came back with a finding stronger than its own brief, and the part
nobody has checked is the part that matters.

MEASURED on alpaca_portfolio/TLT at 2026-09-08T01:42:07Z, read_state
`orders_read` — a CONFIRMED CLEAN READ, so the absence is measured and not a
failed look: of a 72-share short, only 16 shares carry any protective leg.
FIFTY-SIX REST NAKED.

And it is invisible BY CONSTRUCTION. The Alpaca sweep grades SIDES, not
quantity, and the code says so in its own comment
(`stop_qty=None,  # Alpaca grades sides, not qty`). Bybit grades
`covered_qty`; IB grades `stop_qty`/`target_qty`. Alpaca got the two-sided
half of BL-20260816-COVERAGE-IS-ONE-SIDED and never got the quantity half — so
a partly-naked Alpaca position reads as covered and nothing anywhere says
otherwise.

MI-173 explicitly did NOT read alpaca_live. That account is mode: live /
real_money and shares this exact client code, so whether real money carries
the same unmeasurable exposure is UNKNOWN AND NOBODY HAS LOOKED. That is
MI-176's whole question, and it is why this went into the free slot rather
than the queue.

Scoped MEASUREMENT FIRST, THEN DETECTION ONLY. No close, no cancel, no
repair — and explicitly NO re-arm wired off the new grade, because
BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG is what
happened the one time this class was remediated automatically. Its prompt
also requires the `read_state` per account, so an unreadable account is
reported as "we did not look" and never as "nothing is naked" — an
unasserted denominator on a real-money safety question is the exact trap
CLAUDE.md names.

Also recorded, so the findings are not left living only in a PR body:

- MI-173's mechanism, which is NOT the Bybit shape.
  `AlpacaClient.close(self, symbol)` has no qty parameter at all, and
  `execute.close_open_position` validates qty then never passes it. Bybit's
  defect is a RECONCILIATION failure; Alpaca's is an OPERATION failure. A
  Bybit-shaped attribution reconciler would not touch it. Blast radius is
  session-dependent: `closed` defers and cancels nothing; `extended` and
  `regular` cancel every resting order on the symbol and flatten the whole
  symbol. Three things the backlog row never named are now on the row,
  including that `modify_protective` has the identical scope defect on a
  different verb and is filed nowhere.
- That the backlog row's own pinning claim is FALSE on main: the test it says
  pins this does not exist there — it is on the unmerged #11279 branch. On
  main the over-close is unpinned, and if #11279 is rejected that claim
  becomes permanently false.
- MI-174's PR #11311, carrying the addendum's two questions.

* MI-94: enforce register id uniqueness, and fix the session-key collision with a CHECK

The registers already have a row-aware merge driver (MI-76). What nothing
had was the half git cannot do: a SEMANTIC id collision, where a branch
files new work under an id main has already given to something else. To
git that is one changed value at one key, so the merge deletes the row

soaking needs a timer or a soak threshold, or the soak accrues and a held
decision quietly becomes an abandoned one.

The threshold is stated so the row cannot be cleared by impatience or run
forever: >=20 graded rows over >=3 distinct UTC days AND at least one row where
the side-aware grade disagrees with the side-blind sum. A soak in which the new
basis never once disagrees has demonstrated nothing and is not evidence FOR
arming. Deciding NOT to arm clears the row too, and must be recorded as a
decision rather than left looking like a soak still running. Zero rows after
three days is a deploy defect, not a quiet book.

Observation is measured off the VM, not inferred from the merge: the whole file
(1000 requested, 28 returned), spanning 11:32:08Z-11:37:52Z so the writer began
at the restart carrying af9af5e3; all 28 rows annotate/binding false, so the
arming is held on the wire and not only in the default; all three Bybit
accounts graded with the allowlist empty, which is the property that makes
holding the arming satisfiable and the one NETTING_ATTRIBUTION_ACCOUNTS lacked
until 2026-08-09. verdicts_differ is 0 of 28 -- recorded plainly, and explicitly
not read as "the gate is inert", because 5.7 minutes on one day is nowhere near
the declared threshold.

IB protection + breaker, Alpaca capacity read, and one definition of "open" (#10292)

* Over-cover page: name the clientId that submitted each disjoint OCA group

The CRITICAL stop-over-cover page ends with 'cancel the leg that does NOT
match trades.stop_loss'. For the leg it most often names, that is
UN-EXECUTABLE: IB binds cancel rights to the submitting clientId and refuses
a foreign cancel with Error 10147, and clientIds rotate on reconnect. The
page carried no field from which the operator could tell.

Measured live on ib_paper MHG 2026-08-25T20:04Z: trade 4796 LONG 29,
journal stop_loss 6.31207143. oca-protect-465 = STP 6.312 + LMT 7.1415 on
clientId 497 (matches the journal); oca-protect-446 = STP 6.2625 (the
PREVIOUS trail level) + LMT 7.1415 on clientId 597. 58 of resting stop
against 29 of position = 200%.

That pair also names the CAUSE, which no field previously carried: the
second group is the trailing amend's own cancel-and-re-place with the
cancel half refused. Groups accrete one per (rotation, amend) pair, and the
hazard is ordered rather than theoretical -- the stale stop sits BELOW the
live one, so a fall flattens on 465 and then sells 29 more into a naked
short 0.0495 lower.

- ib_client: _readable_client_id (None when unreadable; a genuine clientId 0
  -- TWS's own manual session -- survives rather than being swallowed by a
  falsy check). protection_coverage returns oca_group_client_ids and
  reader_client_id, the EFFECTIVE rotation-aware id, since that is what a
  cancel goes out on. Both keys ship on the flat early return too, so a
  consumer's branch cannot KeyError only when the account is flat.
- order_monitor: _classify_group_owner grades this_session/other_session/
  unknown. 'other_session' deliberately does not assert 'retired' -- a live
  sibling in the 496/497/498 cluster is indistinguishable here and either
  way this client cannot cancel it. 'unknown' is never folded into ours.
- The call site uses cov.get(), so a coverage dict from a client predating
  these keys degrades to unknown rather than raising inside a safety page.

Detect-only is unchanged: it pages, it cancels nothing.

Tests 12 -> 22 in test_stop_over_cover_alert.py, plus 11 new in
test_ib_coverage_group_client_ids.py. Not registered with
collapsed-state-guard, on the BYBIT_HEDGE_MODE_SYMBOLS precedent -- the
guard excludes a producer from its own consumer set and the only branching
code IS the producer, so a row today is met by tests alone or invites a
decorative branch.

(~17:30Z-19:44:43Z, ~2h14m, self-resolved, 6 checks green on 0f71f49a).

The rule asks a per-GROUP question -- does this group hold a correct leg --
where the safety-relevant question is a per-POSITION one: after cancelling it,
is every declared level still covered by a surviving group?

A leg price identical across every group carries no discriminating
information. Counting the tie as a positive match for each group is what
manufactures the ambiguity: the target side cannot separate them, the stop
side separates them by 99 ticks, and the non-discriminating side drives the
verdict.

The proposed change is strictly NARROWER than the current rule -- it refuses
everything the current rule refuses, except where the correct leg survives
elsewhere -- so it cannot reintroduce the 2026-08-20 failure, in which the
cancelled leg was the ONLY one matching the journal.

* A peer-close and a wedge are opposite conditions; stop giving them one response

Tier-2, operator-selected.

_probe_liveness returned a bare bool, so a WEDGE (gateway accepts the socket
and never answers) and a PEER-CLOSE (gateway drops the socket) both reached
_trip_breaker(reason="liveness_probe_timeout") and suppressed EVERY IB call
for 120s. They want opposite responses: a wedge must be backed off from, and
a peer-close is already recovered by the next connect -- the socket is gone,
_is_connected fails, and connect() rebuilds it.

Measured on the live trader journal, episode start 2026-08-24T23:59:09Z,
three consecutive lines with no timeout in them:

  ERROR   ib_insync.client | Peer closed connection.
  WARNING IBClient: liveness probe error ...: ConnectionError: Socket disconnect
  WARNING IBClient: circuit breaker tripped ...; IB calls suppressed for 120s.

74 such episodes over 5.4 days, each blinding every IB leg on an account
holding open positions.

FOUR states, never a bool: ok / skipped / timed_out / disconnected. A test
asserts the probe body contains no `return True` or `return False` at all,
because a caller comparing a bool to a state string is silently wrong rather
than broken. `skipped` is NOT `ok` -- it means we could not probe, so the
caller proceeds but must not stamp _mark_probe_ok; a cached non-verdict is
indistinguishable from a verified one on /api/diag/ib_state.

BOUNDED grace (IB_PEER_CLOSE_GRACE_ATTEMPTS, default 1): a peer-close inside
it raises without tripping; past it the breaker trips normally, under the
reason `liveness_probe_disconnected`. An unbounded reconnect loop against a
sick gateway is the exact failure class the breaker exists for. A successful
connect CLEARS the streak, so the grace covers CONSECUTIVE drops and a slow
trickle of unrelated ones cannot accumulate into a trip on a healthy gateway.

The classifier is narrow on purpose -- type first, message signature as
fallback, and anything unrecognised stays a WEDGE, so the conservative
pre-existing response is the default for every case not positively
identified.

This also closes BL-20260825-IB-BREAKER-FAILURE-REASON-IS-MISLABELLED-AS-A-TIMEOUT,
and closes it the right way: the label was wrong because the CODE could not
tell the two apart, so rewording the literal would have produced a second
guess rather than a fact.

READ SURFACE: /api/diag/ib_state gains last_probe_state, peer_close_streak
and peer_close_grace_attempts. Without them the change is unobservable -- a
permanently-broken grace reads exactly like a working one (the venue_session
lesson) -- and a non-zero streak beside a CLOSED breaker is precisely the
state the grace exists to produce.

ROLLBACK is one env flip: IB_PEER_CLOSE_GRACE_ATTEMPTS=0 restores
trip-on-every-failure. An unparseable value falls back to the DEFAULT, not to
zero, so a typo cannot silently re-arm the condition.

* system-review: make the structural pass mandatory — backlog_classes reads the backlog, this reads the running system

Operator directive 2026-08-24: the review has to look for the bigger
structural problems, not only the per-item defects — "if we see that trades
aren't closing properly, or that there are bugs that are not really resolving
themselves over time because we're just putting on band-aids and we need a
bigger structural fix, those are also things you should be looking for."

The gap was real and this session demonstrated it. backlog_classes (added
2026-08-20) already forces a pattern pass over the BACKLOG, and this session
satisfied it. But the largest findings had no backlog row at all, because they
are only visible as a distribution over live data:

  - 857 of 1324 closed non-backtest trades (64.7%) are closed by cleanup
    machinery, 35.3% by a decision. The M20 exit levers — the entire point of
    the exit-refinement program — have fired 17 times ever (1.3%).
  - The strategy-DECIDED exit path is the UNMEASURED one: 27.0% provenance
    coverage vs the janitor path's 52.0%, with 41.8% of decided closes
    carrying no stamp at all. vwap_cross is 22.9% of real-money closes and
    65.7% of it is unstamped.
  - The pairs sleeve stamps 79 of 79 closes with nothing.

Eight consecutive reviews reported execution-capture as a flat metric without
once asking what it was a symptom OF.

Adds review_coverage.structural_health with three binding rules, each earned:

1. POPULATION IS THE WHOLE HISTORY, not the window. A structural trend is
   invisible in a three-day slice — the window is exactly what let the metric
   stay flat and unexamined across reviews.
2. EVERY FINDING CARRIES A TREND (falling|flat|rising|first_measurement).
   "Is this class shrinking?" is the whole question; a count flat across
   reviews means the fixes are not touching the cause, which IS the complaint.
3. ONE FALSIFIABLE HYPOTHESIS, STATED AND TESTED, with `refuted` exactly as
   legal as `supported`. This session predicted the provenance gap was
   downstream of janitor closes and the measurement said the OPPOSITE; that
   refutation was the most valuable output of the pass. A structural review
   that only confirms what it already believed has tested nothing — RULE ONE
   applied to the review itself. The vocabulary is deliberately binary: an
   "inconclusive" verdict would let a review discharge this by not deciding.

Enforced, not just declared — the failure this key family keeps repeating is a
mandate written in SKILL.md and wired to nothing (account_reachability was
declared mandatory 2026-06-29 and absent from _REQUIRED_COVERAGE_KEYS until
2026-08-20 while the IB gateway flapped unflagged). So: the key is in the
required tuple, has a validator, and has 22 tests exercising the FAILURE path
of every rule, including that both verdicts pass and that four out-of-
vocabulary trend values fail.

tests/test_review_coverage_build_verification.py's clean-payload fixture is
extended, not weakened: it enumerates every required key by design, so it
correctly failed on the new one. 58 tests pass across the three renderer
suites.

Also files the two work items the operator selected, with the measurements
attached so a future session executes instead of re-deriving:
BL-20260824-THE-DECIDED-EXIT-PATH-IS-THE-UNMEASURED-ONE (next work block) and
BL-20260824-PAIRS-SLEEVE-IS-A-SECOND-SYSTEM-THAT-MISSES-INVARIANTS-BY-CONSTRUCTION
(conformance pass, sleeve stays running — it is bybit_1 demo-only).

Guards: claim-basis, impossibility-claims, canonical-doc-coherence and
collapsed-state all pass. No src/, config/, or runtime path touched.

* schema: the report template had drifted FOUR required keys behind the renderer — sync it, and add the detector that catches the next one

Found while adding structural_health, by asking what else builds a
review_coverage payload. comms/schema/system_report_response.template.json is
what CLAUDE.md names as the output schema for /system-review — the shape a
session copies to build its payload — while _REQUIRED_COVERAGE_KEYS in the
renderer is what actually gets enforced. Nothing asserted the two agree, and
they had drifted.

Measured: the template carried EIGHT review_coverage keys against the renderer's
ELEVEN. Missing here: since_last_build_verification, backlog_classes,
ml_output_actionability (all declared 2026-08-20) and unexercised_fixes
(2026-08-24). So the canonical shape actively taught a payload the renderer
would reject, and the only feedback was a --strict failure at render time —
after the review work was already done. That matches what happened in this
session: the renderer rejected the payload four times over shape.

This is the same family as the guards it sits beside — a rule declared in one
place and enforced in another with nothing asserting they agree — which is the
exact recurrence pattern the new structural_health key exists to surface. So it
gets the treatment that class requires: fix the instance AND leave a detector.

- Template synced to all twelve required keys, each with a _comment saying what
  it proves. Its top-level _comment now names the renderer tuple as
  authoritative and this test as the thing that keeps them in step, so the next
  reader knows which of the two to believe.
- tests/test_review_coverage_template_complete.py asserts both directions:
  a required key missing from the template, AND a template key nothing enforces
  (that one reads as mandatory to whoever copies it and quietly is not, so it
  gets filled in with noise). flags_raised is exempted explicitly — it is the
  escalation channel several keys write into, not a coverage key of its own.

Verified the detector FAILS for the right reason, not merely that it passes:
removing backlog_classes from the template — reproducing the actual drift —
makes it fail naming that key. Restored, 62 tests pass across the five suites
that touch the renderer or the template.

Guards: claim-basis and canonical-doc-coherence pass. No src/, config/, or
runtime path touched.

This does not say the cells are wrong — it says the axis as SERVED is
close to constant, which is a question about the parity gap, not about

live ~1%). They must be graded off the live gate's recorded labels.
Cells remain ungraded; squeeze_breakout_4h stays withheld.

against 5 years of training, so part of the gap is market conditions.

got equifinal_no_edge and named the lever: real storage + weather. P1c injects

mean-normalised joint storage+price fit (reuses the optimizer). src/sysdyn/*
stays import-linter-pure (6 contracts kept); all IO in scripts/. New dual
scorecard reports storage fit + price-readout fit (the tradeable quantity) +
identifiability + a go_no_go verdict: invest_deeper only if the price readout

mechanistic-vs-static gate on deeper M29 investment.

P1b + P1c and lands both scorecards via commit-to-main.

Author: Bentzion
Message:
feat(ops): autonomous M5 consumer activation + ship-autonomously rule (#696)

Adds the operator-actions wiring needed to activate the M5
strategy-testing consumer on the VM end-to-end from a labelled
issue (or the workflow UI), and codifies the rule that Claude
should not punt VM activation to a manual SSH session in a runbook.

* `scripts/ops/enable_m5_consumer.sh` (new) — atomic .env edit
  (`M5_CONSUMER_ENABLED=1`) + restart `ict-telegram-bot.service`
  + 30s post-restart `is-active` poll + journal tail + per-run
  audit record. Defers if a `claude-vm-runner@*` is in flight.
  Mirrors the `enable_closed_flat_invariant.sh` pattern.
* `scripts/ops/disable_m5_consumer.sh` (new) — symmetric
  kill-switch flipping the env to `0`.
* `.github/workflows/operator-actions.yml` — adds
  `enable-m5-consumer` + `disable-m5-consumer` to the allowlist,
  the tier table (Tier 2), and the script map.
* `scripts/ops/notify_run.sh` — adds the M5 actions to the
  per-action notify-priority switch (mirrors closed-flat-invariant).
* `docs/claude/operator-actions.md` — extends the action table,
  the dispatcher trust matrix, the per-action notify priorities
  matrix, and the per-action behaviour-detail table.
* `docs/runbooks/strategy-testing.md` — replaces the manual-SSH
  Activation + Kill-switch sections with the autonomous
  operator-action paths; updates the env-var matrix, smoke-test,
  and operator quick-reference table to match.
* `docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md` — adds a new "Ship-Autonomously
  Rule" section: a sprint isn't done when the code lands on main,
  it's done when the change is active in production. VM activation
  is in scope for the sprint that needs it. Manual SSH is the
  documented exception, not the default.

The drive-by here was the operator's note: the M5 close-out left
"set M5_CONSUMER_ENABLED=1 on the VM" as a manual operator step in
the runbook, even though the existing operator-actions workflow
makes that fully scriptable. Sprint hygiene tightened so future
milestones don't repeat the pattern.

Author: Bentzion
Message:
ops: add Velotrade DXtrade secrets to rotate_api_keys notebook (#340)

Single canonical place for the operator to drop Velotrade credentials —
matches the existing Bybit per-account pattern so the cred-rotation flow
stays consistent across exchanges.

Three new optional Colab Secrets:
- VELOTRADE_API_KEY_1     — DXtrade API key for prop_velotrade_1
- VELOTRADE_API_SECRET_1  — matching API secret
- VELOTRADE_BASE_URL      — sandbox vs prod toggle (e.g. https://demo.dx.trade)

The names match accounts.yaml::prop_velotrade_1::api_key_env exactly —
phase-2's resolve_credentials() derives _SECRET_1 from _API_KEY_1
automatically, and velotrade_client_for() reads VELOTRADE_BASE_URL from
env (or accounts.yaml::base_url override).

Behaviour:
- Cell 3 (load secrets): Velotrade keys added to OPTIONAL list — safe
  to leave unset; the not-fully-configured gate from phase-2 already
  handles that gracefully.
- Cell 4 (build .env): VELOTRADE_API_KEY_1 + VELOTRADE_API_SECRET_1
  flow through PER_ACCOUNT_KEYS; VELOTRADE_BASE_URL flows through a
  new VELOTRADE_CONFIG_KEYS list. All three are conditional on the
  Colab Secret being present so missing values don't render empty
  lines into the .env file.
- Markdown header: VELOTRADE rows added to "Optional Colab Secrets"
  table; BREAKOUT rows marked DEPRECATED (kept so existing operator
  Secrets don't error). New "Velotrade onboarding flow" section
  explains the safe ordering: drop secrets → run notebook →
  /accounts_status flips configured=True → fill in DXtrade SDK
  contract → add strategies to YAML.

Smoke-tested cell 4 in isolation: all three keys land in the rendered
.env when present, stay out cleanly when absent (no empty=blank lines).

Docs/notebook only — no live-route changes.

Message:
feat(accounts): Velotrade phase-2 — DXtrade integration infrastructure + 'not fully configured' account state (#337)

Refocused mid-session per operator clarification: build the integration
infrastructure (not hook up a specific account); add a generic
not-fully-configured account state so accounts with missing creds load
into the unit, surface in /accounts_status, and emit a diagnostic ping
on any action that requires creds.

What ships
- DXtradeClient (src/units/accounts/dxtrade_client.py) — real ctor +
  cred validation; place/cancel/status/balance methods raise
  NotImplementedError("contract pending") until the operator drops
  the API contract. MissingCredentialsError is the canonical signal.
- velotrade_client_for(account) in clients.py — mirrors
  bybit_client_for / binance_conn_for; returns None on missing creds.
- VelotradeAPI.place(order, dry_run=False, client=…) accepts an
  injected DXtradeClient and dispatches retCode-style live placement.
- execute._submit_order velotrade branch: real call structure with
  MissingCredentialsError on missing client + retCode handling.
- multi_account_execute: routes exchange == 'velotrade' through
  velotrade_client_for; not-fully-configured message names the env var.
- TradingAccount.configured + configured_reason fields, populated by
  load_accounts() via resolve_credentials(). Surfaced in status().
- prop_velotrade_1 in accounts.yaml lost enabled: false — the
  not-configured layer keeps it inert (empty strategies + missing
  creds + stub SDK methods + four existing safety rails).

Tests
- 20 new in tests/test_velotrade_infrastructure.py covering ctor
  validation, factory cred resolution, loader configured flag, and
  end-to-end coordinator path (live + missing creds → ping fires;
  dry-run → no ping).
- TestVelotradeExecutor + TestRealAccountsYaml in
  tests/test_prop_risk_manager.py rewritten for the new vocabulary.
- 264 passed across the accounts/coordinator regression sweep.

Live-mode check
- scripts/check_dry_run_in_diff.py: clean.
- bybit_1 / bybit_2 unchanged. prop_velotrade_1 ships with empty
  strategies — per-account routing filter blocks any signal.
- Touches src/units/accounts/* + src/core/coordinator.py (rule 3 list)
  → flagged for PM review; PR stays draft despite green CI.

Architecture rules
- Only accounts unit + coordinator touched. No new cross-unit imports.
- execute_pkg remains the single canonical live-order entry point.
- DB unit + bot untouched. Strategies untouched.

Resolves CP-2026-05-03-02 in docs/claude/checkpoints/CHECKPOINT_LOG.md.

Author: Bentzion
Message:
S-023 PR3: API failure pings with direct response (#245)

Every Bybit/Binance API call that fails now routes through
outcomes.report at ERROR with the direct API response (retCode +
retMsg, HTTP status, or exception type + message) attached in ctx.
The operator gets a Telegram ping for each new failure
fingerprint, rate-limited by the existing PR1 dedup + hourly cap.

What changed
------------
src/runtime/api_reporting.py (new, ~150 LOC):
  - report_api_failure(exchange, op, account_id, error, response,
    exception): single chokepoint for every API failure site.
  - _redact_for_telegram: strips long tokens (>=18 chars),
    api_key/api_secret/token/Authorization KV pairs, and
    "Bearer <token>" headers before responses go to Telegram.
    Defers to existing log_redact for Telegram-bot-token shapes.
  - _excerpt: JSON-renders dicts (readable), falls back to
    str/repr, truncates to 500 chars after redaction.
  - Never raises (ping-on-failure must not crash the host).

Wired into:
  - data_loaders.account_balance_with_diagnostic — both the
    retCode path and the exception path now ping with the
    direct response in ctx.
  - data_loaders.account_open_positions — exception path pings.
  - units/accounts/execute._submit_order — exception path pings
    (still re-raises so risk manager sees the exception too).

Each report_api_failure call is wrapped in a defensive try/except
so a broken reporter cannot break the host call site.

Tests
-----
tests/test_api_reporting.py (21 cases):
  Redaction: long tokens, kv api_key, Bearer prefix, camelCase
  apiKey, non-string input, short IDs preserved.
  Excerpt: json rendering, truncation, None handling, unjsonable
  fallback, redacts credentials in dicts.
  report_api_failure: routes through outcomes with right
  action/status/level/ctx, exception_type, response excerpt
  redacts creds, swallows internal failures.
  Integration: retCode -> ping, exception -> ping, missing-creds
  -> no ping (already shown in /accounts_status).

278 passed, 0 failed in the full S-022 + S-023 + adjacent suite.

Message:
S-013 M3 PR #2: flip require_session from no-op to enforcement (PM REVIEW) (#180)

⚠️  AUTH ENFORCEMENT — flagged for PM review per CLAUDE.md.
    Do not self-merge. After this lands, the dashboard endpoints are
    default-deny and require a valid bearer JWT signed with the VM's
    JWT_SIGNING_KEY whose 'email' claim equals ALLOWED_EMAIL.

Replaces the M2/M3 PR #1 no-op decorator pattern with a FastAPI
dependency:

  src/web/api/auth.py
    - require_session is now an `async def require_session(request)`
      dependency.
    - PUBLIC_ROUTES = {"/api/auth/login", "/api/health"} — every other
      route default-denies. Adding to PUBLIC_ROUTES is a code change.
    - 401 'invalid_session' for missing/bad/expired/wrong-sig/alg=none
    - 403 'email_not_allowlisted' if a valid token's email no longer
      matches ALLOWED_EMAIL (operator de-allowlisted post-issuance)
    - 500 'auth_unavailable' if ALLOWED_EMAIL env is missing — no
      env-var name leaked
    - 401 also when JWT_SIGNING_KEY is missing (decode fails closed)

  src/web/api/routers/status.py, src/web/api/routers/pnl.py
    - Switched from `@require_session` decorator to
      `_session: dict = Depends(require_session)`.

Tests:

  tests/test_web_api_status.py — full enforcement suite:
    - happy path with valid bearer
    - 503 paths still work (with valid token)
    - missing Authorization → 401
    - non-Bearer scheme → 401
